sources.entry: Flying Carpet - cross-platform file transfer over ad-hoc wifi, like AirDrop but for Mac/Windows/Linux.

summary.one_liner: Flying Carpet is a cross-platform app for sending files directly between Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, and Windows over ad hoc WiFi hotspot or a shared local network, without internet.
summary.what_it_does: It transfers files between two devices either by having one device host an ad hoc WiFi hotspot that the other joins, or by having both devices join the same existing WiFi or wired network. In hotspot mode, Bluetooth can exchange the hotspot credentials automatically after a pairing code is confirmed; otherwise the host displays a password and QR code. In shared network mode, the receiver shows a one-time password with a QR code, and the sender types or scans it to find the peer and start the transfer. Each transfer is encrypted with a Noise NNpsk0 handshake keyed from the transfer password via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations, with fresh keys per transfer. The desktop app is built with Tauri and Rust; the Android and Apple apps are separate native builds in the same repository.
use_cases: send large files between phone and computer without internet
transfer files between Mac and Windows or Linux machines
move files without a flash drive or network share
share files over a shared WiFi or wired network
transfer files from iPhone to Windows PC
how_to_run: Install Rust, then run `cargo install tauri-cli`
On Ubuntu 22.04+, install dependencies: `sudo apt install build-essential curl wget file pkg-config libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libdbus-1-dev librsvg2-dev`
Run `cargo tauri dev` for a development build or `cargo tauri build` for release artifacts
iOS/macOS: open `Apple/iOS/FlyingCarpet.xcodeproj` or `Apple/macOS/FlyingCarpet.xcodeproj` in Xcode (requires a Mac and your own signing team)
notable: Shared Network mode uses an existing WiFi or wired network, with a one-time password and QR code for discovery; no Bluetooth needed in this mode
Hotspot mode can exchange WiFi credentials over Bluetooth after a pairing code is confirmed
Noise-based encryption with per-transfer keys for forward secrecy
Published as Android APK, iOS app, Linux AppImage/deb/rpm, macOS zip (also Homebrew), and Windows MSI/exe (also winget)
Version 10 is not compatible with version 9 or earlier
caveats: Apple devices cannot start hotspots programmatically, so Apple-to-Apple transfers need a shared network
Hotspot mode disables the wireless internet connection on the device; VPN should be disabled on both devices
Android needs version 10 (API 29) or later and does not work on some Xiaomi, MIUI, or HarmonyOS devices; Linux AppImage/deb/rpm need Ubuntu 22.04+ or glibc 2.35+
